newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger amid U.S. bond gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger amid U.S. bond gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Wednesday, pulled higher by but underperforming their U.S. counterparts, amid an absence of significant Canadian economic data or news, analysts said.
"U.S. Treasuries are up big even with lots of supply coming. You've got lots of supply looming in Canada as well," said Hank Cunningham, a bond trader with First Marathon Securities.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.30 at C$102.95 to yield 7.736 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which rose 22/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 81 basis points from 78 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.

The only major event in the Canadian bond market today was the a new issue from the province of Alberta this morning, analysts said. The province issued a C$350 million, 6.125 percent bond due October 4, 2001, said lead manager RBC Dominion Securities Inc.
"We had an Alberta issue which sold right out with a very narrow spread," said Cunningham. The issue was priced just six basis points over the Canada 7.0 percent, 2001 bond.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.46 to C$98.77 to yield 7.170 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 13/32 to yield 6.69 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds was 48 basis points, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.86 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.05 percent.
Analysts said the decline in the yield on the cash bill since early yesterday afternoon reflects renewed speculation that the Bank of Canada will cut short-term interest rates.
